results.content:

Want to improve the discoverability and organization of your digital collections? Metadata is key to making archival materials accessible, and Dublin Core is one of the most widely used metadata standards for describing digital archives, museum collections, and historical records.

This recorded webinar explores how archivists and digital collection managers can implement Dublin Core metadata in Omeka, a leading open-source platform for digital exhibits and collections.

In this session, you'll learn:

✔️ What Dublin Core is and why it’s essential for metadata standardization
✔️ How to apply Dublin Core fields in Omeka to improve searchability and organization
✔️ Best practices for metadata entry, including controlled vocabularies and interoperability with other systems
✔️ Real-world examples of Dublin Core in action for libraries, archives, and museums
✔️ How to enhance digital exhibits with structured metadata to improve user access

Whether you’re an archivist, digital collections manager, or Omeka user, this webinar will help you maximize the potential of Dublin Core metadata and optimize your digital archives for discoverability.

📌 Watch now to improve metadata workflows and take your digital collections to the next level!

Interested in Omeka? Shoot Emma an email at emma@backlog-archivists.com
https://www.backlog-archivists.com/

Title: Adding fields to Dublin Core - Omeka S - Omeka Forum
I’m in the process of testing an import from DSpace to Omeka S via the DSpace connector. DSpace uses additional Dublin Core fields that aren’t in Omeka’s DC vocabulary, as well as a different format…e.g Omeka S (dc:spatial) and DSpace (dc.coverage.spatial). Right now, what happens is that the spatial coverage metadata from DSpace duplicates when coming into Omeka, populating the coverage and the spatial coverage fields. Is there a way to change the Omeka S Dublin Core vocabulary to match the nested format of DSpace, or am I better to change the fields in DSpace to remove the nesting? I think this is actually just a function of how the DSpace Connector module works: when it sees those DSpace-style “dc.coverage.spatial” terms, it maps them to both “coverage” and “spatial.”. I’ve also tried importing into dspace with the dc.coverage.spatial and with dcterms:spatial, and the items with dcterms don’t seem to be bringing the metadata into omeka. The “dcterms” issue is also a problem on the connector side, I think: it only knows how to handle “dc” elements… examples of usage of dcterms-namespaced metadata on the DSpace side of things would be helpful for us improving that support. results.title: Omeka s vs Dspace for creating institutional repository - Omeka S - Omeka Forum
results.content: # Omeka s vs Dspace for creating institutional repository. You have selected **0** posts. is omeka a good choice for creating institutional repositories for universities of technology. Omeka S is a web publishing platform and is not a preservation grade repository. It is possible to use it as a front end for a DSpace or Fedora instance, but it is not a substitute for those preservation services associated with those repository systems. For your information, the French university Université Toulouse Jean-Jaurès 13 chose Omeka S as an institutional repository instead of e-prints and d-space, too complex and hard to maintain. It’s called Dante 66, for Dépôt et archivage numérique des travaux étudiants. Students can deposit their works and thesis via the modules Guest and Contribute. Each librarian of the faculties can moderate the records of their own students. The files and metadata are reversed in a long time archive and in various public repositories.
